senses.gloss: m. (contr. of בי רבי, belonging to a school of an eminent teacher, v. בֵּי 4) B’rabbi, B’ribbi, title of scholars, most frequently applied to disciples of R. Judah han-Nasi and his contemporaries, but also to some of his predecessors, and sometimes to the first Amoraim, v. אֲמוֹרָא.
units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 85a:9">B. Mets. 85ᵃ</cite> <he>אסמכיה ב׳</he> he gave him the title of B’rabbi (a scholar of Rabbi Judah).
<cite ref="Chullin 11b:8">Ib. 11ᵇ</cite> <cite ref="B01165"><he>ברבי</he></cite>; <cite ref="Makkot 5b:10">Macc. 5ᵇ</cite> <he>בריבי</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 100).

<cite ref="Shabbat 115a:7">Sabb. 115ᵃ</cite> <he>רבן גמליאל ברי׳</he> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 13:2">Tosef. ib. XIII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 14:2">XIV</cite>), 2; Mass. Sofrim V, 15 only <he>ר׳ גמ׳</he>) R. Gaml. son of R. Judah han-Nasi.
<cite ref="Eruvin 53a:18">Erub. 53ᵃ</cite> <he>רבי אושעיא ברי׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>ברב׳</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. notes 70; <cite ref="Eruvin 80a:8">80</cite>) R. O. scholar of Rabbi Jud. han-N.—
<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 1:18">Sifré Deut. 1</cite>, end <he>יהודה ברב׳</he> (<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 792:1">Yalk. ib. 792</cite> only <he>יהודה</he>).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:5:14">Y. M. Kat. III, 82ᶜ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 100:7">Gen. R. s. 100</cite> <he>חד בר׳ אמר</he> a student (Amora) recited &c.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 8:10:5">Y. Sot. VIII, end, 23ᵃ</cite> <he>לית רבי ב׳</he> [insert <cite ref="A00516"><he>או</he></cite>] not even a teacher or a student was exempt. [<cite ref="Sanhedrin 17b:6">Snh. 17ᵇ</cite> <he>רמי בר ברבי</he>, read <cite ref="B01197"><he>ברוכי</he></cite>.]
